notes:
dashy 0.7.0

Three weeks and 677 commits since 0.6.0. The through-line is that a dashboard
now knows what kind of thing it is, measures itself, and can act on what it
finds.

Project-shaped dashboards, closed. The archetype spec ran to Phase 7
(Judgment): composition rules per archetype, a declared-versus-inferred badge,
a drift check, and a settings surface for setting one. What 0.6.0 shipped as a
registry is now the thing that decides what a dashboard is made of.

Metrics and KPIs. A measurement contract, a metric series written and read on
a schedule, and a metrics widget. Dashboards carry numbers now, not only lists.

Adding a project, from inside the app. A door that registers a folder, names
its root, and repoints one that moved, instead of hand-editing config.

The file view became a working surface. Todos render and edit in place, verbs
act on a line, nested lists fold, and the line numbers are owned rather than
inferred.

Grid Mode and the Iron Man skin. A second skin taken through v3, plus a
segmented control, an aperture reveal, and a display face that holds at grid
density.

Phone widths. dashy is habitable on a phone: stacked cards, a calendar that
pays for its own space, and a nav that fits.

Chat gained topics and a dispatch lifecycle, and two silent defects in the
composer are fixed.

CI became self-hosted, and a red test became actionable. Builds run on this
machine's own runners. A failing test files itself as an inbox item, can be
queued as a fix proposal, and closes itself when it goes green again. The
proposer proposes; it never merges.

Security hardening. PUT /api/files accepts markdown and nothing else, the
write-surface allowlist closed its symlink and extension gaps, and
refuse_client_path now covers every client-facing read and write surface.

Also in this release: every browser popup is a styled dialog, settings and
diagnostics were neatened end to end, dashboard configuration can be edited in
batch, the version is single-sourced from this tag, and dashy exposes an MCP
tool server to Claude Code sessions.

Upgrading needs no manual step. The eight new schema migrations (027 through
034) apply on first launch, and generated data reads from both its old and its
new home during the migration window.

Known and shipping unfixed, for the third release running: the Windows build
bundles keyring without its backends, so provider credentials fall back to
dashy's own file store rather than Credential Manager. Nothing is lost and the
fallback is the designed one.
